# English template for translating the Darkest Dungeon accessibility mod's own spoken strings.
#
# GENERATED by Mod\gen-lang-template.ps1 from Mod\src\core\axstrings.inc -- do not edit this
# copy; edit the .inc and regenerate. English itself is built into the mod, so this file is
# NEVER loaded: it is the starting point for a new Mod\lang\<language>.txt.
#
# HOW TO USE
# 1. Copy this file to Mod\lang\<language>.txt, named after the game's INTERNAL language name
#    (french.txt, spanish.txt, italian.txt, polish.txt, russian.txt, czech.txt, ...).
# 2. Replace the English text after each = with your translation. Translate the WHOLE line
#    naturally; word order may differ from English freely.
# 3. Keep every printf placeholder (%d, %s) exactly as in English and in the same order. A
#    line whose placeholders differ is rejected at load and stays English. %% is a literal %.
# 4. Delete or comment out (#) any line you do not translate -- it stays English either way.
# 5. Save as UTF-8. Send the file to the mod's maintainer; it is compiled into the mod by
#    Mod\build.ps1 and takes effect at the next game start in that language.
# Full format notes: Mod\lang\README.txt. A finished example: Mod\lang\german.txt.

# ---- MOD TUTORIALS: the mod's own help dialogs (core/modtutorial.cpp, 2026-10-10) ----
MT_TITLE_P1=Welcome to Darkest Dungeon! Mod tutorials like this will automatically appear in many areas of the game to help you learn how to play. You can also view them by pressing F1 for context-sensitive help.
MT_TITLE_P2=General Controls: Use the arrow keys, D-pad, or left joystick to navigate through the user interface. Enter, or A on the controller, to activate. Escape, or B on the controller, will take you back a screen, cancel an action, or open the pause menu.
MT_TITLE_HINTS=Control hints: The mod will provide hints on the commands available to you for each screen or control. You can turn these off in mod settings or by pressing F2.
MT_TITLE_P3=Reading pop-ups: Pressing comma will re-read the active pop-up or dialog box.
MT_TITLE_P4=Reading tooltips: Tooltips hold detailed information on heroes, enemies, items, skills, and more. By default, they are read automatically, but this can be configured in mod settings or by pressing F3. You can read them line by line with Ctrl+Up and Down arrows. Some tooltips have multiple sections, and you can move between them with Ctrl+Left and Right arrows. On controller, hold the left trigger and navigate with the D-pad or left stick.
MT_TITLE_P5=Searching: You can search most areas of the game by pressing Ctrl+F.
MT_TITLE_P6=Settings: You can access mod settings by pressing F10 from anywhere in the game. Game options are found in the pause menu. Some options, such as game and music volume, use sliders, which you can adjust with the left and right arrow keys.
MT_TITLE_P7=Support: The readme on GitHub features guides to help you get started with every area of Darkest Dungeon. If you encounter bugs, have feedback, or need help, you can reach me on Discord. Links to the readme and my Discord server can be found in mod settings.
MT_TITLE_P8=If you do not wish to see further messages like this, select the checkbox below to disable mod tutorials.
MT_OPTOUT_FMT=Do not show mod tutorials, checkbox, %s.
MT_OK=OK, button.
MT_OPTOUT_HINT=You can still open one with F1, or turn them back on in mod settings.
MT_NONE_HERE=No mod tutorial for this screen.
MT_CLOSED=Closed.
MT_CAMP_P1=Campaign screen: There are nine campaign save slots, each with three buttons to the right (delete, DLC, and mods). At the top of the screen is a button for the Butcher's Circus, a free-to-download competitive multiplayer mode.
MT_CAMP_P2=Starting a new game: Activate an empty slot to start a new game. If you own any DLC, you will then select which content to add for that campaign. Afterwards, you will select a difficulty, and finish by naming your estate. Activate your newly-created save to begin.
MT_CAMP_P3=Naming your estate: The edit field starts with the word Darkest auto-filled, and has a max of 10 characters. You'll hear the updated entry as you type or delete text. Press Enter to finish and create your new save.
MT_CAMP_P4=Deleting a save: There is a Delete button to the right of each save slot, or you can press Delete on the keyboard. You will be asked to confirm before deleting.
MT_CAMP_P5=DLC content: You can press Shift+Enter or use the button to the right of an existing save slot to view the DLC enabled for that campaign or enable more content at any time. Once DLC has been enabled, however, it cannot be disabled for the rest of that campaign.
MT_CAMP_P6=Enabling mods: Press Spacebar or use the button to the right of an existing save to open the mod manager for that campaign, where you can enable or disable mods. Note that disabling a mod mid-campaign is not recommended, as it could corrupt your save file.
MT_DUNG_P1=Dungeon view: Most of the game will take place in side-scrolling dungeons. Your characters will be lined up on the left side of the screen, facing right, towards where objects, enemies, and doors will appear. This means your party is numbered right-to-left, while enemies, who face left, are numbered left-to-right.
MT_DUNG_P2=Heroes: Your party can contain up to four heroes. You can change the active hero by pressing Q/E (LB/RB on controller). The active hero is the one that will interact with and be affected by curios, treasure, and traps. You can open the active hero's character sheet at any time by pressing C (X on controller). There is a summary of their current status within tooltips on each character in the party.
MT_DUNG_P3=Interaction: Press W to interact with curios, obstacles, and treasure, enter doors, and disarm traps (LT+A on controller). You can also activate whatever has focus.
MT_DUNG_P4=Light: Press L to read the current light level and its effects. Light will drop over time and must be replenished with torches. T will light a torch, Shift+T will dim it one level, and Ctrl+Shift+T will snuff it out completely. On controller, hold LT and press Y to light a torch, B to dim it, and hold LT+B to snuff it out.
MT_DUNG_P5=Log: As you progress through the dungeon, various things will happen to your heroes. You can press the period key (LT+RB on controller) to open the combat log, which will show everything that has happened. Page Up and Page Down will move through the entries ten at a time, and pressing the Delete key will allow you to clear the log entirely.
MT_DUNG_P6=Map/Inventory: The dungeon map and your party's inventory share the same panel on screen. Tab moves your focus to that panel and switches between them. You can also press M or I to open either the map or the inventory directly (LT/RT on controller).
MT_DUNG_P7=Movement: Dungeons are made out of a series of rooms connected by hallways. You will use the map to select which room to travel to next, and will then walk your party through the hallways, using D to move forward and A to move back (right stick on controller). Forward will always be to the right, towards the destination you selected.
MT_DUNG_P8=Navigation assist: Shift+A/D will move you forward/back one tile at a time, so that announcements don't cut off and you do not walk past anything. Inside a room, it will move you to within reach of any curios or treasure in the room with you. It will also prevent you from stumbling into traps that your party has successfully spotted on the ground.
MT_DUNG_P9=Party order: Your party may get shuffled around in combat. You can move a hero by pressing Enter (A on controller) on the hero you want to move, then choosing their new position. To quickly reset to the default party order after a battle, you can press Shift+Enter (hold A on controller) on any hero.
MT_DUNG_P10=Quests: Above the dungeon view, you will find the quest panel, containing your current goal, as well as a button to either retreat from combat, abandon the quest, or complete the quest and return to town. You can also press G to jump to your goals directly, or press Shift+Escape as a shortcut to retreat, abandon the quest, or return to the Hamlet (depending on context).
MT_DUNG_P11=Review mode: You can press Alt+1 through Alt+4 to quickly review who is in each rank of your party. During combat, Alt+5 through Alt+8 will review who is standing where on the enemy side.
MT_DUNG_P12=Skills: You can find the active hero's skills on the action bar below the dungeon view. Pressing the tilde key (to the left of the number 1) will also jump you there directly from wherever you are. During combat, you can use 1 through 5 to quickly select a skill to use, based on its position on the action bar. 5 will always be the move action.
MT_MAP_P1=The map: The map is where you can see the layout of the dungeon and choose your next destination. How much you are able to see depends on your party's scouting.
MT_MAP_P2=Use the arrow keys to move the cursor from room to room. Pressing Enter on a room adjacent to your party's current location will move them into the adjoining hallway.
MT_MAP_P3=Hold Ctrl and use the arrow keys to move the cursor tile by tile along hallways (LT+D-pad or left stick on controller).
MT_MAP_P4=Pressing Home will return the cursor to your party's current location (LS click on controller).
MT_BAG_P1=The inventory: The inventory consists of 16 slots, arranged in two rows of eight.
MT_BAG_P2=Activating an item will allow you to use it on one of your heroes. During combat, each hero can only use one item on themselves per turn.
MT_BAG_P3=Activating a trinket will allow you to equip it to one of your heroes, provided they have an empty trinket slot.
MT_BAG_P4=You can rearrange items in your inventory with the spacebar (LS click on controller).
MT_BAG_P5=You can remove an item from your inventory with the Delete key (hold Y on controller).
MT_CS_P1=Character sheet: This is where you can view all of the information about your heroes, equip trinkets, and swap out their combat and camping skills.
MT_CS_P2=Up/Down to move through the different sections. Left/Right moves through the info on each row.
MT_CS_P3=Quirks: Traits that affect that character. You can have up to 5 positive and 5 negative quirks. When you gain a new quirk that would take you over the limit, it will replace another quirk at random.
MT_CS_P4=Base stats: Your hero's maximum hit points, accuracy, protection, and so on. Any special modifiers will be shown as a tooltip.
MT_CS_P5=Equipment: Weapon and armor unique to each class, which affect that hero's base stats and can be upgraded in town.
MT_CS_P6=Trinkets: Special items that you equip to your character. Each character can have up to two trinkets, which are equipped by pressing Enter on a slot or from the inventory.
MT_CS_P7=Combat skills: The actions your hero can take in combat. The tooltip for each shows its effects, what ranks it can be used from, and what ranks it can target. They all use your base stats for damage, accuracy, and crit chance, but a particular skill may modify these. For example, a skill that says 30 percent damage would deal 30 percent of whatever your base damage is. The combat skills section also includes a summary of how many of the currently equipped skills can be used from each rank and what ranks they can target.
MT_CS_P8=Camping skills: Actions the hero can take while camping. The tooltip for each skill describes its effects, who it can target, and how much time it will take to perform.
MT_CS_P9=You can reassign skills by pressing Enter to select and deselect them in the order that you want them to appear on the action bar. Alternatively, you can press the numbers 1 through 4 to quick assign a skill to a particular slot.
MT_CS_P10=Diseases: Negative traits that can be acquired in various ways while adventuring, which must be cured in town.
MT_CS_P11=Manage: Options to rename or dismiss a hero from your roster.
MT_HAM_P1=The Hamlet: This is where you'll manage your heroes, items, and other resources between adventures.
MT_HAM_P2=You can press Tab and Shift+Tab to move between the different sections of the town interface (RT and LT on controller).
MT_HAM_P3=Hamlet Locations: The map is presented in list format. Each building has a specific function and most of them can be upgraded. There are character-key shortcuts to open each building directly (see the full list in the readme or mod control settings).
MT_HAM_P4=Roster: This is where you can view all of your heroes, arranged in a vertical list. At the top is a horizontal bar with your roster limit and options to sort your roster. You can also manually rearrange the heroes by pressing the spacebar to pick one up, moving to the desired slot, and then pressing the spacebar again to drop it (click the left stick for drag and drop on controller).
MT_HAM_P5=Resources: Shows how much gold, heirlooms, and other resources you have. The Trade heirlooms button can be used to exchange one type of heirloom for another.
MT_HAM_P6=Trinket inventory: Press the I key to open an inventory of any trinkets you have that are not equipped to a character. Above the grid are options to unequip trinkets from all your heroes or to sort the items in the grid. You can press Enter on a trinket to equip it to a hero. You can sell unwanted trinkets for gold by pressing Shift+Enter.
MT_HAM_P7=Activity log: Press period to open a record of what happens each week that passes.
MT_HAM_P8=Town events: Most weeks you return from adventuring, you will have a town event, which can have different positive or negative effects. You can re-read these windows with comma while they are open, close them with Escape, and they can be reopened at any time by pressing Shift+period.
MT_HAM_P9=Embarking: Press E to embark on your next quest.

# ---- MOD TUTORIAL: the EMBARK screen ----
MT_EMB_P1=Quest Planning: On this screen, you will select which quest to attempt and assemble your party of heroes.
MT_EMB_P2=Press Tab and Shift+Tab to move to the different sections.
MT_EMB_P3=Quest map: Move Left/Right to browse the locations on the map. Move Up/Down to view the quests at that location. Additional information about each quest is available in its tooltip. Press Enter to select a quest.
MT_EMB_P4=Party lineup: The ranks are numbered right to left, matching how they will appear in the dungeon. Press Enter on a slot to open the roster, where you can select who you want to assign to that rank. Selecting the same hero currently in a given rank will remove them from the party. Use the spacebar (LS click on controller) to rearrange the heroes in your party without removing them.
MT_EMB_P5=Provisions: Press E (RS click on controller) to advance to the provisioner, where you can purchase supplies for your expedition.

# ---- MOD TUTORIAL: the PROVISIONING screen ----
MT_PROV_P1=Provisioning: This screen is where you will purchase supplies for your adventure.
MT_PROV_P2=Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move through the different sections.
MT_PROV_P3=Provisioner: The main area is broken into two columns. The shop's inventory is on the left and yours is on the right. You can purchase or sell back a single item with the Enter key or an entire stack with Shift+Enter.
MT_PROV_P4=Quest info: The quest info panel shows you information about the quest you selected and your party's scouting chance.
MT_PROV_P5=Party lineup: You can review and manage heroes in your party on this screen as well.
MT_PROV_P6=Embarking: Press E (RS click) to finish your preparations and begin the quest.

# ---- MOD TUTORIAL: a BUILDING interior ----
MT_BLDG_P1=Buildings: The interface for each building is generally organized into rows and columns. While inside a building, you can press the U key (LT on controller) to open the upgrades menu. Use Page Up and Page Down to quickly swap between the different buildings.

# ---- MOD TUTORIAL: a CAMP ----
MT_CAMPING_P1=Camping has two phases. First, you'll select how much food you want to eat, which is a simple list of options. The second phase, the skills phase, is where your heroes can use camping skills to heal, reduce their stress, and buff themselves for what lies ahead.
MT_CAMPING_P2=During the skills phase, you will hear how many respite points you have in the readout for the dungeon view. Each camping skill will cost a number of these points. Once you have 6 or less remaining, you'll see a button to rest on the action bar, which will finish camping and return you to the normal dungeon.
MT_CAMPING_P3=Use Q/E (LB/RB on controller) to change the selected hero and find their camping skills in the action bar under the dungeon view. You can check their tooltips to learn more about what each skill does.

# ---- MOD TUTORIALS: THE BUTCHER'S CIRCUS ----
MT_BANNER_P1=Banner Designer: Your banner is like your player emblem, which other players see during a match. It is made up of six pieces, which you unlock as rewards for completing matches.
MT_BANNER_P2=This screen is laid out fairly simply. Focus arrives in a vertical list of tabs, one for each piece of your banner. Under these tabs are a button to randomize your selections and a button to apply all changes. To the right of the tabs is a grid, showing the different pieces for the selected tab.
MT_BANNER_P3=Press Ctrl+Enter to save your changes.
MT_BANNER_P4=Press R for a random banner.
MT_BANNER_P5=Press the B key to speak a full summary of your current banner design.
MT_DUEL_P1=Dueling Grounds: This is where you can challenge other players to a private match. It has two columns: your friends list on the left, where you can press Enter on any of your online friends to send them an invite, and a section on the right where you can invite a player by typing in their Steam ID. Alternatively, you can create a lobby ID, which will connect you if you both type in the same thing.
MT_DUEL_P2=Once connected, you will select a party and press E to mark that you are ready. Once players are ready, the match will begin.
MT_PRIZE_P1=Prize Box: This is where you can see how much prestige you've accumulated, the rewards you've unlocked, and what you'll unlock at later levels. It is a simple grid. Up/Down to move through the prestige levels, Left/Right to browse the details of the rewards for that level. Pressing Enter on a banner piece will take you to preview it in the banner designer.
MT_RANK_P1=Rankings Board: This is where you can see your multiplayer rank and match history. At the top, it lists your current rank, what rank is next, and your progress towards achieving it. If you win a match, you'll gain skulls which progress you towards the next rank. Losing a match can cause you to lose skulls and even drop down a rank.
MT_RANK_P2=Below your rank info is a list, with two tabs at the top: Matchmaking history for public matches, and Challenge history for your record in the dueling grounds. Use Left/Right arrows to switch tabs, Up/Down to navigate the list. On each row you'll hear the outcome of the fight, the heroes in both parties, and who was killed in the fight.
MT_RING_P1=The Ring: This is the main area of the Butcher's Circus, where you build a party, equip them with trinkets, and send them to fight. Everything here applies to private matches through the dueling grounds as well.
MT_RING_P2=The party lineup and commands for it are identical to the singleplayer campaign. Enter to select, C to view character sheets, spacebar to rearrange.
MT_RING_P3=Equipping trinkets also works identically to the campaign. Press Enter on the trinket slots on a hero's character sheet, or press I to open the trinket inventory, press Enter on a trinket, and then select who you want to equip it on.
MT_RING_P4=Press E when you are ready to start a match with another player (RS click on controller). The first match you fight will be a tutorial against an AI opponent.
MT_RING_P5=You can press P to start a practice round or replay the tutorial (LB on controller).
MT_RING_P6=Pressing L opens a reference of the different league ranks (RB on controller).
